_source: awk run with sh -c in containers of these images (docker run -d, one docker exec per case as uid 0, a fresh /tmp/w per case), 2026-10-21, Docker 29.8.2 on linux/arm64: the order of `for (k in a)` with large arrays. Programs: 1 integers 1..N and 2 strings "k" i for N 10, 47, 48, 49, 63, 64, 65, 100, 500, 609, 610, 611, 1000; 3 integers and strings "s" i mixed (N 64, 100, 1000); 4 every even key deleted (N 100, 1000); 5 inserted from N down to 1; 6 a lookup of every key in reverse before the loop; 7 numeric strings "" i alone, before and after the integers. awks: gawk 4.0.2 (centos:7), gawk 4.1.4 (debian:9 with the gawk package of archive.debian.org), gawk 5.1.0 (rockylinux:9), gawk 5.2.1 (debian:12 with the gawk package; the default awk of debian:12 is mawk), mawk 1.3.3 (debian:10), mawk 1.3.4 20200120 (ubuntu:22.04), 20240123 (ubuntu:24.04), 20250131 (debian:13), the awk of BusyBox 1.36.1 (busybox:1.36.1-musl). `meta` names each case, `groups.version` the version calls (not run by the tests). Nothing normalised; a second run of a sample of 72 cases gave the same output (none of these cases is volatile).
